paper_title: Parallelised Bayesian Optimisation via Thompson Sampling
mechanistic_insights: This paper is purely computational and does not study any chemical reactions. It develops a Bayesian Optimization algorithm.
Asynchronous parallel Thompson Sampling (asyTS) is highly effective when function evaluation times have high variability, as it minimizes worker idle time.
Synchronous parallel Thompson Sampling (synTS) may be preferred if evaluation times are deterministic and equal, as it uses more complete information for each batch of queries.
The inherent randomness of Thompson Sampling is generally sufficient to ensure diversity in parallel evaluations, and explicit diversity-enforcing schemes may not improve performance.
The performance of parallel Thompson Sampling with 'n' evaluations distributed among 'M' workers is theoretically shown to be nearly as effective as performing 'n' evaluations sequentially.

quantitative_outcomes.best_performing_conditions: The paper does not describe a chemical reaction. The best performing computational algorithm was asynchronous Thompson Sampling (asyTS) for optimizing functions with variable evaluation times, as demonstrated in hyperparameter tuning of a convolutional neural network.
quantitative_outcomes.notes: This is a computer science paper on a general optimization algorithm. It does not contain any experimental chemistry. The relevance to cross-coupling is that the described algorithm could potentially be used to optimize such reactions, but the paper itself does not do so.
